newsitem.title: UK: British Conservatives slip one point in new poll.
newsitem.headline: British Conservatives slip one point in new poll.

text.p: With a general election approaching, support for Britain's ruling Conservative Party has slipped one point to 31 percent while opposition Labour is unchanged at 49 percent, according to an opinion poll.
The NOP poll for the Sunday Times gave the minority Liberal Democrats 13 percent, also unchanged from last month.
If the results were carried into a general election, Labour would have a 200-seat majority in the 659-seat House of Commons (lower house), the Sunday Times said.
Prime Minister John Major must hold a general election by May 22 and his Conservatives appear to have little chance of narrowing the 20-point opinion poll lead Labour have held for two years.
Major's hope is that Britain's slowly improving economy will restore voters' faith in his party, which has been in power for 18 years, but the poll suggested this was unlikely.
It indicated that 40 percent of voters believe Labour would run the economy more efficiently than the Conservatives -- down from 41 percent a month ago and from as high as 54 percent last winter.
Twenty-eight percent of voters polled believe the Conservatives would be better at economic management, unchanged over the past 12 months.
